thesis: ASML fell ~11.8% over 60 calendar days (1784.87 -> 1574.65), with a 6% single-day drop today tied to a sector-wide semiconductor selloff after Anthropic's CEO publicly called for the AI industry to slow model-capability development, spooking chip-supply-chain names broadly (ASML, SK Hynix, Micron, Lam Research all fell in sympathy). This suggests the move is sentiment/macro-driven rather than a company-specific deterioration: ASML's own fundamentals in the same window improved — it beat Q2 EPS ($8.82 vs $7.98 est) and revenue estimates, raised full-year 2026 guidance, and JPMorgan reported (after meeting ASML's CFO) that 2027 EUV capacity is nearly sold out and the company is exploring 110+ machines for 2028 on 'very very strong' AI demand. The strongest counter-case — that this reflects real doubts about AI capex durability rather than just sentiment — doesn't fully invalidate the read since ASML's order book and customer bookings (extending to 2028) are forward, multi-year commitments unlikely to unwind on a single sentiment-driven day, but it does mean the setup can't be called a clean company-specific catalyst.
invalidation: Thesis invalidated if the sector risk-off move is followed by confirmed order pushouts or cancellations from foundry customers (TSMC, Samsung, Intel) rather than just a sentiment-driven pullback, or if ASML's 2027/2028 capacity commentary is walked back.

thesis: BAC shares fell ~5.9% today on more than double normal volume (2.06x average) after CEO Brian Moynihan told an industry conference that Q3 investment banking fees will land at $1.6-1.8B, over 10% below last year and short of the ~$2B Street consensus, and that trading revenue will be roughly flat versus Q2's 33% surge. This is a specific, company-disclosed data point (not a rumor or analyst guess), but it is forward guidance about a quarter that hasn't closed yet — closer to an 'ahead of earnings' setup than a confirmed, already-realized event. The strongest counter-case is that this week's widely-expected Fed rate hike should structurally help BAC (management itself has said a 100bp short-rate rise adds roughly $800M to annual net interest income); that doesn't change the near-term read because the guided IB/trading softness lands in the same quarter and the NII benefit from a hike accrues gradually over 12 months, not immediately.
invalidation: Thesis invalidated if Q3 results (due mid-October) beat the guided IB fee range and show trading revenue held up better than 'flat', indicating the guidance was overly conservative.

thesis: GEV fell ~15.6% over 60 calendar days (1036.22 -> 874.66), including a 6.5% drop today as part of the same broad AI-slowdown-driven selloff hitting chip- and power-infrastructure names after Anthropic's CEO urged the industry to slow AI development. The picture is mixed rather than clearly resolved: GLJ Research initiated coverage today with a Sell rating and a $470 price target (roughly half the current price), while Jefferies raised its target to $1,185 just three days ago and kept a Buy, and GEV's underlying demand story (116 GW of gas turbines on order/reserved, now booking 2031 deliveries) remains intact per recent reporting. With a fresh bearish analyst call, an offsetting bullish one, and a sector-wide sentiment shock all overlapping, there's no single dominant, resolved read on today's move.
invalidation: Thesis invalidated if the GLJ Sell call and broader AI-slowdown selloff are followed by confirmed order pushouts from GEV's own customers, or conversely if sell-side coverage converges bullish and the stock stabilizes, showing today's move was purely sentiment noise.

thesis: CNQ (held) remains supported by its Aug 6 Q2 report, a confirmed, already-disclosed beat: adjusted EPS of C$2.15-2.19 vs. a C$2.01 consensus and revenue of C$14.74B vs. C$13.36B expected, followed by CIBC raising its target to C$75 from C$70 on Aug 27 citing strong free-cash-flow generation and deleveraging. Shares have also benefited from a crude-oil rally tied to Iran-related supply disruption, hitting a fresh 52-week high ($52.31) on Sep 10. The strongest counter-case is that the rally is largely a macro oil-price story that could reverse quickly if Gulf tensions de-escalate; that doesn't invalidate the read here because the Q2 beat and CIBC's post-earnings target hike were framed around company-specific execution (cost control, deleveraging, FCF) independent of the price of crude, so the fundamental case doesn't depend on oil staying elevated. No litigation, dilution, insolvency/liquidity, or leadership-turnover items surfaced in this run's search, and no earnings or other binary catalyst falls before the next review.
invalidation: Long thesis invalidated if oil prices reverse sharply on Hormuz/Iran de-escalation and the next quarterly update shows CNQ's own production costs or output slipping, undermining the case that the move is fundamentally rather than just macro supported.
